newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds unchanged after U.S., outlook quiet.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds unchanged after U.S., outlook quiet.

text.p: Danish bond prices were more or less unchanged in early trade on Monday after rising briefly at the opening, with dealers predicting a quiet, low turnover day ahead of central bank meetings in Germany and America.
"The focus is on the Fed and the Bundesbank. The market is still unsure what the Bundesbank will do about repo rates tomorrow while nobody sees the Fed changing rates," one dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 traded virtually unchanged from Friday's close at 112.40, with yield at 6.09 percent,R at 0735 GMT.
The seven percent 2007 bond, due to become the benchmark on September 1, stood at an unaltered 105.29, yielding 6.27 percent.
The 2007's 10-year yield gap with Germany widened one point to 61 basis points. The crown was at 3.8090 per mark, the same as Friday's close. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33-969652
